Article Title: Lot of videos, hours in the nets and a solid game plan: How KL Rahul cracked the New Zealand code
Article Text:
India's KL Rahul (AP/PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Wellington: "Feels really awesome, actually, to be able to achieve something like that," said KL Rahul , visibly pleased after achieving the rare feat of scoring Test centuries in all four SENA countries as an opener. He reached the milestone on Day 3 of the first Test against New Zealand and was delighted to make a substantial contribution in India's first innings. Rahul arrived in New Zealand early to begin his preparations, following his usual routine, and also squeezed in an India A game before the Tests. His returns weren't particularly encouraging, and the subsequent ODI series didn't give him much time at the crease. However, Rahul made the most of his net sessions in Christchurch, Auckland and Wellington."I didn't get a lot of runs in that India A game. But I used the time in the nets and tried to figure out how I could give myself the best chance to succeed in these conditions. There's a lot of Test cricket under me, a lot of experiences, good and bad. I just had very clear plans before I came here as to how I wanted to play. And I'm happy that I could go out there and do that and get the results in the first innings. That's performances and runs," Rahul said at the end of the day's play.New Zealand is now the fifth country in which Rahul has reached the three-figure mark, and this century will arguably taste the sweetest. Twelve years after making his Test debut, this was his first outing in this part of the world, and he certainly left his mark. Rahul arrived with a plan, stuck to it and never deviated from the methods that have brought him immense success in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle.Rahul enjoyed considerable success in England last year, looked solid in Sri Lanka and has now carried that consistency into New Zealand. The build-up to the tour revolved around the challenges of batting in these conditions. When the teams arrived at the Basin Reserve, the talk surrounding the 15mm grass cover took centre stage. Add to that the possibility of strong winds and persistent cloud cover.All the chatter, however, did little to distract Rahul, who had done extensive homework by watching videos of recent Test matches. His research convinced him that scoring runs here was very much possible, while the examples of Joe Root and Harry Brook gave him the confidence he needed."I've been thinking about Test cricket in New Zealand for the last six or seven months, trying to do my homework, trying to see the guys who have scored runs here and how they've been able to achieve that. And once I got the opportunity, if I ticked all those boxes, then it becomes slightly easier when you play the game."I watched the last few years of Test cricket here. England played here, Australia played here, West Indies were here recently. So, yeah, I just pulled out some videos and asked the analysts to send me footage of guys who've scored runs here. Joe Root was there, Harry Brook scored a lot of runs. I just watched how they went about it. It gave me a little confidence that it's not impossible to score runs in New Zealand. It requires a very clear game plan," Rahul explained.There were passages of play when Rahul became the cushion absorbing all the pressure, but he never looked out of place. He weathered the storm, allowed his partners to take charge whenever required and remained steadfast at the other end. He was at peace with his methods and had remarkable clarity of mind. There were a few nervy moments after he walked out to bat, including a close LBW appeal and some inside edges, but Rahul dug deep to bring up his 10th overseas hundred.Interestingly, only three of his 13 Test centuries have come at home."I will buy Glenn Phillips a few drinks after the game for not reviewing that. Those were the slowest 15 seconds of my life. Kept hoping people would listen to GP," Rahul said, recalling the moment when he was struck on the pads and given not out, only for New Zealand to decide against reviewing the umpire's decision.At the Basin Reserve, Rahul featured in three significant partnerships that have put India in a strong position in the Test match. His arm is still sore from the blow he took, but after months of preparation and homework delivering the desired results, he will have little trouble getting a comfortable night's sleep.
Article Summary: KL Rahul scores century as India beat New Zealand in first Test. Rahul becomes fifth player to score Test century in all four SENA countries. India batsman had done extensive research on New Zealand conditions. Rahul says he will buy Glenn Phillips a few drinks after the game.

Article Title: Shubman Gill and the art of spotting his father in the stands
Article Text:
Shubman Gill (Pic credit: BCCI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

WELLINGTON: When Shubman Gill reached his half-century with an authoritative pull, the Indian captain raised his bat towards the stands behind square leg. He has a knack for spotting his father, Lakhwinder Gill, dressed in his “lucky” white kurta-pyjama, no matter how crowded the stands are. Gill Sr. can make the task a little challenging with his habit of changing positions, but on Saturday, he knew exactly where his family would be seated.When India resumed batting on Day 2, Lakhwinder was seated right behind the bowler's arm. But as the wind picked up, he moved in search of some warmth from the sunshine and joined his wife, Keart Gill, on the benches near the museum. By the time Gill walked out to bat, the Indian captain would have known that his father's position was now fixed. The sunshine was just what Lakhwinder needed as the temperature dipped.It was an innings of complete control from the captain, who missed out on a deserved hundred by just two runs but ensured India were firmly in a position of dominance. He added 91 runs with KL Rahul before stitching together a breezy 100-run partnership with Rishabh Pant , maintaining the tempo throughout. Gill brought up his half-century off just 66 deliveries and kept India's momentum going even after the dismissals of Devdutt Padikkal and Rahul.There was a sense of urgency, but Gill never allowed desperation to creep into his 146-ball knock. He kept bisecting the field with precision and wasn't afraid to go aerial whenever the pressure began to build. New Zealand tried a double trap, stationing two catchers on the off side to capitalise on mistimed drives while packing the field for the pull and hook shots. Gill wasn't perturbed. He made room to dispatch the short deliveries through the covers and was particularly strong through the leg side.By then, New Zealand had realised that Gill wasn't falling for any bait and would have hoped for a lapse in concentration to breach his defence. A moment of uncertainty arrived with a close LBW appeal, but replays suggested an inside edge, prompting the umpire's call to be overturned. Rishabh Pant urged him to review the decision. Just when the cameras were ready to capture a second raise of the bat, possibly followed by another acknowledgement towards the same section of the stands, an anti-climax awaited.Gill fell for 98. It would have been his first Test hundred on New Zealand soil. A Jacob Duffy delivery, angling in, breached his defences, and a frustrated Gill began the long walk back to the dressing room.His father, Lakhwinder, shared the disappointment. But he will be back in the stands in Christchurch, wearing the same white kurta-pyjama, hoping his son spots him once again.
Article Summary: Gill missed out on a deserved hundred by just two runs. He added 91 runs with KL Rahul before stitching together a breezy 100-run partnership with Rishabh Pant. Gill brought up his half-century off just 66 deliveries and kept India's momentum going.

Article Title: Harry Kane ruled out for months after suffering ankle ligament injury in Bayern Munich draw
Article Text:
Bayern Munich's Harry Kane suffers an injury during (AP)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

England captain Harry Kane is set for an extended spell on the sidelines after sustaining a ligament injury in his left ankle during Bayern Munich's 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne on Friday.The 33-year-old suffered the injury following a challenge from Cologne defender Joel Schmied. The incident occurred as Schmied attempted to intercept a low delivery from Michael Olise, reaching the ball first before making contact with Kane 's left leg in his follow-through near the back post.Kane was left in considerable pain and remained on the ground for treatment. Although he managed to get back on his feet and briefly continued, the Bayern striker was eventually forced to leave the pitch, hobbling off with the assistance of two physiotherapists.Bayern subsequently confirmed the extent of the injury, with medical examinations revealing damage to the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle. The German champions also indicated that their leading forward would be unavailable for the next few months."Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich's Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich's medical department.The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months," the club said in a statement.The injury comes as a major setback for Bayern, given Kane's importance to the side since arriving from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023. The England international has been the club's standout attacking figure, registering 156 goals in 161 competitive appearances while helping them secure two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup.Kane has also enjoyed significant individual success, becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or last month. His long-term future at the German club appeared settled after he signed a contract extension just two weeks ago, keeping him in Bavaria until June 2029.However, his latest injury will now force Bayern to cope without their prolific forward for the coming months.
Article Summary: England captain Harry Kane is set for an extended spell on the sidelines after sustaining a ligament injury in his left ankle. The 33-year-old suffered the injury during Bayern Munich's 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne on Friday. The incident occurred as Schmied attempted to intercept a low delivery from Michael Olise.

Article Title: 'He's not the only one': NZ bowling coach backs Jacob Duffy after expensive outing against India
Article Text:
Jacob Duffy. (Image: AP)

Oram highlights Duffy's hard work and commitment

Duffy continues to work on his game despite success

Day 3 report: Rahul, Gill and Padikkal put India in control

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe India is in a strong position to win the Test match against New Zealand? Yes, they have a strong lead. No, anything can happen in cricket. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Brief scores: New Zealand 368 all out; India 486/4 (KL Rahul 136, Shubman Gill 98, Devdutt Padikkal 80, Rishabh Pant 55*). India lead by 118 runs.

New Zealand bowling coach Jacob Oram has thrown his weight behind Jacob Duffy after the fast bowler endured a difficult outing on day three of the first Test against India at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. Duffy conceded 181 runs in his spell, including seven no-balls, as India took control of the contest with a commanding batting display.Despite the expensive figures, Oram insisted that one difficult day should not overshadow Duffy's recent performances and consistent hard work. The New Zealand coach also pointed to the pacer's achievements over the last two seasons, saying he has earned enough credit to move past a disappointing performance.Oram said the 30-year-old pacer should not be judged on the basis of one expensive performance, especially after the consistency he has shown over the past two seasons."Jacob Duffy is fine. I mean, you should know, we try not to get too high when things are good and we try not to get too low when things haven't gone your way. So today, if you just look at the scoreboard, it's not his day."But he's had way too many good days in the last two seasons for one day to suddenly put him in the depths of despair.So he'll be okay. At the same time, he knows he's got areas to work on and improve, but he's not the only one in the dressing room," Oram said during the post-day press conference.Oram also pointed out that Duffy's commitment to improving his bowling has remained consistent, even during the most successful phases of his career.According to Oram, Duffy continued working on different aspects of his bowling even while collecting individual honours and enjoying opportunities at the highest level."I don't want to go into specifics, to be honest, just because the dude went for a few runs. But I say again, guys are always working on stuff. Even before this Test, he was working on stuff. Even last season, when he won the Sir Richard Hadlee Medal and the Players' Cap, he was working on things."I know right now I'm sitting here and you can say it's lip service because he's had a bad day, but the guy is always working hard. I think when you see where he's got to with those awards, with the IPL opportunity he got and with some other stuff coming his way, that's how these guys stay where they are because he's always working on stuff – his run-up, delivery stride and wrist position. But even if he's bowling well, we're still working on things," he added.Meanwhile, India produced a dominant batting performance on the third day of the opening Test to take a commanding 118-run first-innings lead against New Zealand.Resuming their innings at 159/1, India finished the day at 486/4 in 125 overs, with KL Rahul leading the charge through a magnificent 136 off 290 deliveries. The opener struck nine boundaries and two sixes to register his 13th Test century.Devdutt Padikkal provided excellent support with an impressive 80 off 175 balls, sharing a crucial 165-run partnership with Rahul for the second wicket. Kyle Jamieson eventually broke the stand by dismissing Padikkal.Rahul later combined with captain Shubman Gill for another important partnership before Nathan Smith ended his innings.Gill continued India's dominance with an aggressive 98 off 146 deliveries, striking nine fours and two sixes. However, he fell agonisingly short of his 12th Test century after Duffy bowled him in the final over of the day.Rishabh Pant also made a significant contribution, remaining unbeaten on 55 off 62 balls. He shared a 100-run partnership with Gill to further strengthen India's position.New Zealand, who had posted 368 in their first innings, struggled to contain the Indian batters on a pitch that increasingly favoured batting. Jamieson and Smith picked up one wicket each, while Duffy finished with one wicket for 180 runs according to the day's scorecard.
Article Summary: Jacob Duffy endured a difficult outing on day three of the first Test against India at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. Duffy conceded 181 runs in his spell, including seven no-balls, as India took control of the contest with a commanding batting display. India finished the day at 486/4 in 125 overs, with KL Rahul leading the charge through a magnificent 136. Devdutt Padikkal provided excellent support with an impressive 80 off 175 balls, sharing a crucial 165-run partnership with Rahul for the second wicket.

Article Title: Legal battles mark Indian Olympic Association election race

NEW DELHI: With December 5 polls for the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) drawing closer, legal challenges to the electoral college are piling up even as sporting and political circles work through alliances, arithmetic and a consensus slate for key posts.Nominations for IOA office-bearers’ posts for the coming 2026-2030 term begin Sunday, and closed-door meetings in political corridors have intensified in the national capital. Sources said hopefuls have consulted their political masters, while some have been advised to step aside.Authorities are understood to favour a consensus presidential candidate, avoiding a contest for the top post, with similar efforts for other key officebearer positions — like what had happened during the 2022 elections. Consensus has reportedly emerged on some names, but back-channel talks continue, and surprises remain possible as the deadline nears.In the legal corridors, federation officials from boxing, golf and table tennis have approached the Delhi High Court seeking inclusion of their representatives in the electoral college, allowing them to vote and contest. Sources informed that the boxing federation received relief on Thursday. The court directed the returning officer to hear its grievances. Golf and table tennis matters are also expected to come up.

Article Title: Forfeitures could be a lesson for Total Chess organisers
Article Text:
Magnus Carlsen

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BUDAPEST: Magnus Carlsen repeated his Houdini act on Wednesday, going missing from the table for the Fast Classic game against Bibisara Assaubayeva in the ongoing Total Chess Pilot event here, after ensuring that he could not lose. This time, he was not alone. Abhimanyu Mishra and Richard Rapport followed the leader into forfeiting their Fast Classic games, the former against R Vaishali.The Indian Grandmaster was left ruing a missed opportunity for some game practice ahead of her Women's World Championship match against Ju Wenjun. Mishra now runs into Vaishali's brother R Praggnanandhaa in a contest for the 21st place. Rapport could not have beaten Haik Martirosyan even if he had won the Fast Classic.Anish Giri and Alireza Firouzja will compete for the crown over the next two days. Although Giri comfortably sailed past Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, Firouzja needed the Armageddon to beat Fabiano Caruana.The story of the knockouts, however, has been the forfeitures.In this event where all the three formats of the game are coming into play to zero in on the 'complete chess champion', a maximum of 20 points is up for grabs across four games of Blitz, two of Rapid and one of Fast Classic.The Fast Classic, which gives the winner 8 points, happens last. So, if a player gains at least 10.5 from Blitz (1 point for a win and .5 for draw) and Rapid (4 points for the winner and 2 for a draw), he might well consider it futile to play the Fast Classic. Although the question of ethics might come up, a player cannot be faulted for the forfeiture.In a World Championship match of 14 games, with one point for a win and .5 for a draw, the contest ends as soon as a player reaches 7.5 points.Organisers of Total Chess could well take this leaf out of the World Championship book. "We will take the players' inputs after this pilot event before going forward," Total Chess CEO Kjell Madland had told TOI earlier.The pilot event is being organised to iron out the creases, and one is clearly showing.(The writer is in Budapest on an invitation from Total Chess)
Article Summary: Magnus Carlsen forfeits Fast Classic game against Bibisara Assaubayeva. Abhimanyu Mishra and Richard Rapport follow the leader into forfeiting their Fast Classic games. Anish Giri and Alireza Firouzja will compete for the crown over next two days.

Article Title: Orissa HC questions Hockey India secretary general’s power to convene meetings
Article Text:
Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: The Orissa High Court has questioned whether Hockey India’s secretary general can convene Executive Board (EB) meetings without the orders or consent of federation president Dilip Kumar Tirkey, observing that the probable answer under its bye-laws is “not in the affirmative”.The observations came in the detailed order dismissing Hockey India’s plea to vacate the Nov 6 interim stay on its election process. The stay on the proposed elections continues, while the main writ petition remains pending. The order, passed on Wednesday, was made available on Thursday.Justice RK Pattanaik examined the authority under which Hockey India’s 119th and 120th EB meetings were convened. The 119th meeting, held in Tirkey’s absence, approved the proposal to conduct the elections and appoint an electoral officer. The 120th was convened by the secretary general and chaired by EB member Tapan Kumar Das Examining Hockey India’s bye-laws, the court said no provision had been brought to its notice permitting the secretary general to convene meetings without the president’s orders or consent. It observed that the secretary general functions as the “Administrative Executor” of the president’s decision rather than as an independent convening authority.The court, however, stopped short of finally deciding the legality of the decisions taken at the meetings, saying the issue would be considered while disposing of the main writ petition.It clarified that its observations were confined to the interim applications.The court also noted that some other state units were in default but had not received notices similar to the one issued to the Hockey Association of Odisha (HAO), saying HAO’s apprehension of being singled out “may not be entirely misplaced”.It further observed that initiating the process to reclassify HAO from a permanent member to an associate member when Hockey India elections were proposed could give rise to an allegation of mala fide and had created a “trust deficit” between the parties.
Article Summary: The Orissa High Court has questioned whether Hockey India’s secretary general can convene Executive Board (EB) meetings without orders or consent of federation president Dilip Kumar Tirkey. The probable answer under its bye-laws is “not in the affirmative’, the court said. The observations came in the detailed order dismissing Hockey India's plea to vacate the Nov 6 interim stay on its election process.

Article Title: Digboi Golf: Three-way lead at top after Round 3 sets up exciting final day
Article Text:
Yuvraj Singh

DIGBOI: Yuvraj Singh joined overnight leaders Om Prakash Chouhan and Raunil Kukar at the top as the 26th Indian Oil SERVO Masters Golf tournament looks poised for an exciting final day at Digboi Golf Links with a three-way lead for the title after the third round here on Thursday.Overnight joint leader Chouhan (67-68-70), 40, carded a two-under 70 – with six birdies, a double-bogey on the par-3 10th and two bogeys – to retain his share of the lead.The 28-year-old Kukar (70-65-70), from Bengaluru, the other overnight joint leader, also returned a two-under 70 comprising five birdies and three bogeys to remain at the top.Kapurthala’s Yuvraj (68-70-67), 25, who began the day tied fourth and three shots off the lead, fired a five-under 67 featuring seven birdies and two bogeys to join the overnight leaders. He made six of his birdies in two sets of three consecutive holes, first from the fifth to seventh and then from the 14th to 16th.Bangladesh’s Md Razu (69-70-68) climbed from tied eighth to fourth at nine-under 207 following a four-under 68 with five birdies and a lone bogey on the par-4 eighth.The biggest jump of the day belonged to Mumbai’s Aryaman Aditya Mohan (73-70-65), who climbed from tied 25th to tied fifth at eight-under 208 with a seven-under 65 featuring an eagle on the par-5 seventh, eight birdies and three bogeys.Chandigarh’s Akshay Sharma (75-67-66) joined Aryaman in tied fifth after a six-under 66 comprising an eagle on the seventh, six birdies and two bogeys.However, the title looks to be former champion Chouhan’s to miss continued to put himself in contention for another title.“I played well today. My putting was good as well, although I struggled a little with my putting tempo on the 10th hole,” Chouhan said of his third-round show.The 11-time PGTI winner, former European Challenge Tour winner and 2023 PGTI rankings champion, however, said he would do the planning for the final day only after waking up on Friday.“It depends on my mood and the vibe after I wake up in the morning. If I worry about it from now on, I won’t be able to sleep tonight,” he told TOI.Kukar, playing his sixth consecutive PGTI season, came close to his maiden title at Nava Raipur Open in September, where he finished joint runner-up, one shot behind Khalin Joshi.Kukar, who made a bogey on the final hole along with Chouhan, said, “OP and I both made bogeys on the last hole, which was unfortunate, but we have to take things as they come. I’m very grateful to be where I am right now. There is still a lot of work to do and a few things to prepare for tomorrow.”Yuvraj, playing his fourth consecutive PGTI season, will be chasing his maiden title with his current best finish on the tour being the third place at PGTI Players Championship in April 2025.“It feels good to be at the top of the leaderboard. I think what worked for me today was simply sticking to my process and doing what needed to be done,” said the 25-year-old.The undulating fairways and small greens at Digboi Golf Links have tested the field and will be ready with challenges on Friday to crown the winner of this Rs 1 crore prize money event.(The writer is in Digboi on an invitation from DP World PGTI)
Article Summary: Yuvraj Singh joins overnight leaders Om Prakash Chouhan and Raunil Kukar at the top. 26th Indian Oil SERVO Masters Golf tournament looks poised for an exciting final day at Digboi Golf Links. Overnight joint leader Chouhan carded a two- under 70 to retain his share of the lead.

Article Title: Rawalpindi Test: Pakistan end two-year drought as Sri Lanka suffer historic low with four straight away series defeats
Article Text:
Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by 8 wickets in the Pawalpindi Test. (Pic credit: SLC)

Sri Lanka's overseas struggles deepen

Babar praises youngsters as Mendis looks ahead

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A new-look Pakistan side ended a two-year wait for a Test series triumph, overpowering Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the second Test in Rawalpindi on Friday to clinch the two-match series 1-0. The defeat extended Sri Lanka's miserable overseas run, leaving them with four successive away Test series losses and a calendar year without a single Test victory for the first time since 1997.Chasing a modest target after restricting Sri Lanka to 316 in their second innings, Pakistan raced to 90/2 in just 13 overs during the first session on Day 4. Aamer Jamal provided the finishing flourish with an unbeaten 34 off 22 balls, smashing five fours and a six, while Azan Awais remained not out on 32.The victory was Pakistan's first Test series win since beating England at home in October 2024. It was also only their third win in 11 matches in the current World Test Championship cycle.Pakistan captain Babar Azam was particularly pleased with the way his relatively inexperienced side responded to the challenge."Very satisfying, the way the team performed. We had a young team, many players grabbed their opportunities.The environment in the dressing room is very positive, we just need to stay stable and focus on the game. All the players gave 100% to their roles and that was nice to see," Babar said.The series defeat added another unwanted chapter to Sri Lanka's recent Test record. Their last overseas series victory came against Bangladesh in March 2024, and they have now lost four consecutive away series.The Islanders will also finish 2026 without a Test victory for the first time since 1997. Pakistan, meanwhile, have won three of their last four Test series against Sri Lanka, whose previous series triumph over Pakistan came in September 2017.Sri Lanka's troubles in Rawalpindi began in the first innings when Pakistan's seamers bowled them out for just 98 inside the first two sessions on the opening day. The visitors conceded a massive 227-run first-innings lead, leaving themselves with a mountain to climb.They showed greater resistance in the second innings, with Milan Rathnayake remaining unbeaten on 66 to help extend the contest. However, Mohammad Abbas, who claimed 3/55 in the innings, ended the resistance by trapping Asitha Fernando lbw in his first over on Friday.Abbas, who was named both Player of the Match and Player of the Series, said his performance had been overdue."The performance was due, I spoke before the series and the challenges before it, still have to take a 5-wicket haul, hopefully I will do it. I assess the conditions, make sure that my economy is low and it helps the other bowlers as well. I only advised them to hit the areas well, Saqib became unfit unfortunately, that made my responsibility more," he said.Pakistan's victory was particularly encouraging given the number of fresh faces in the squad, with four players making their debuts during the series. Babar singled out wicketkeeper-batter Ghazi for making the most of his opportunities and also credited fast bowler Razaullah's pace and first-innings contribution."If you have a bowler who can bowl at 145 kmph, it gives you confidence. His spell in the first innings was vital and that was one of the main reasons for our series win today," Babar said.Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis acknowledged that his side's poor first-innings batting had proved costly."Honestly, we didn't bat well in the first innings, including me. I got out at a crucial time. We bowled well and batted well in the 2nd innings. Bowling wise, I thought we hit the areas well," Mendis said.He also thanked Pakistan for hosting the team during a tour that included a 2-1 T20I series defeat and a loss in the ODI tri-series final."We've stayed here for more than one month, we enjoyed Pakistan and have had positives in both Tests. The fast bowlers bowled well and I'm happy with the improvement. Looking forward to the tour of New Zealand. Hopefully, I will be back here in the PSL or some other tournament. I thank Pakistan for hosting us, we enjoyed our stay here," he added.
Article Summary: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the second Test in Rawalpindi. Pakistan won the two-match series 1-0 to claim their first Test series win since beating England in October 2024. Sri Lanka have now lost four consecutive away Test series.

Article Title: Mohammed Siraj snub under scanner as India pacers struggle! Kotak defends team selection after New Zealand fightback in 1st Test

Mohammed Siraj and Sitanshu Kotak

NEW DELHI: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defended the decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand, insisting that the selectors and team management had picked the best possible combination despite the pacer's omission coming under scrutiny after a difficult opening day for India's bowling attack at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday.With Jasprit Bumrah doing most of the damage, India's other pace options struggled to make an impact as New Zealand recovered from 70/5 to reach 243/5 at stumps. Henry Nicholls remained unbeaten on 113, while Glenn Phillips was six runs short of a century at 94 not out, the pair putting together an unbroken 173-run stand for the sixth wicket.Siraj's absence was particularly noticeable as Anshul Kamboj, playing in his place, managed just one wicket for 57 runs in 18 overs. Prasidh Krishna went wicketless, conceding 58 runs in 16 overs, while Akash Deep returned figures of 1/33. Bumrah, meanwhile, finished with 3/52 from 17 overs.Asked about Siraj's omission at the post-day press conference, Kotak backed the selection call and said the team management had considered the conditions and opposition while settling on its best XI."I think at a time they pick the team, they think about the best XI, and that’s what played. Nothing wrong with Siraj, they thought of the best possible XI and played.Sri Lanka was different conditions. Not wrong decision to drop Siraj," Kotak said.He also explained the thinking behind India's bowling combination, pointing to the different skills offered by the pace attack and the decision to include Washington Sundar because New Zealand had four left-handers in their XI."On current attack: Two bowlers swing the ball well and two seam the ball well. And have pace. When you pick XI, you think about all days. Picked Washi because of four left-handers in opposition XI," he added.The decision, however, came under the spotlight as Bumrah repeatedly troubled the New Zealand batters while the other Indian bowlers struggled to maintain pressure after the new ball lost its shine.Kotak also defended Prasidh, whose expensive spell included several boundary-scoring deliveries, saying the Karnataka pacer was an attacking option who could be expensive while searching for wickets."Prasidh is an attacking bowler and he can go for runs. People like it when he picks wickets, and they don’t when they go for runs," Kotak said.India had made an impressive start after winning the toss, with Bumrah removing Tom Latham, Devon Conway and Daryl Mitchell before dismissing Tom Blundell to reduce the hosts to 70/5. Kamboj also struck early, but Nicholls and Phillips turned the contest around with a patient yet increasingly assured partnership.Kotak felt India had an opportunity to make further inroads, particularly with a chance to dismiss Nicholls going down."The pitch helped with the new ball, the weather was good and sunny so it dried out. We should have taken that catch, Rishabh Pant went for the catch but it was close to Devdutt Padikkal," he said.Nicholls eventually reached his 12th Test century, while Phillips continued to counter-attack as India's bowling attack lost its early bite. Bumrah was the only bowler who consistently threatened, leaving India with plenty to ponder after surrendering control of a day that had begun so promisingly.
Article Summary: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defends decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand. Kotak says selectors and team management had picked the best possible combination despite Siraj's omission. Jasprit Bumrah was the only bowler who consistently threatened New Zealand's batting line-up.

Article Title: India clinch historic lawn bowls series in New Zealand
Article Text:
(From left) Dinesh Kumar, Reshma Kumari, Pinki Singh and Sunil Bahadur after winning the trophy in Auckland on Wednesday

India completed a remarkable turnaround to clinch the three-match lawn bowls series against New Zealand with a 3-2 victory in the deciding test at Royal Oak Bowls in Auckland on Wednesday.Having lost the opening test before levelling the series with a comeback win on Tuesday, the Indian team produced another composed performance to seal the trophy on New Zealand soil.The experienced Jharkhand duo of Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur gave India a winning start, defeating their New Zealand opponents 9-7 in the men’s pairs. New Zealand hit back in the women’s pairs, where Reshma Kumari and Pinki Singh went down 2-5.India regained the advantage in the mixed fours as the quartet grabbed a crucial 7-5 victory. The visitors then sealed the overall test by winning the first mixed pairs contest 5-2. Although New Zealand claimed the second mixed pairs match 7-4, India had already secured an unassailable lead and with it the test and the series.The triumph completed a stunning recovery after India lost the opening test and found themselves adapting to unfamiliar conditions in Auckland. According to Dinesh, belief in their own abilities proved crucial to the turnaround.“We know that if we play our natural game, we can challenge any team in the world. We showed that here. We kept reminding each other to play our best and leave everything on the green. Everyone gave their all, and we achieved our goal,” he said on Wednesday.For Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki, the key to India’s revival lay in the unity shown by the four-member contingent. “The best thing was our unity. None of us made excuses about being tired, lacking sleep or facing difficult conditions. All four of us played as one team. We fought together, came back together and eventually won the series together,” Pinki said.Sunil, meanwhile, underlined the significance of winning the trophy away from home.“The biggest satisfaction comes from winning on New Zealand’s home turf. Winning in India would have been special, but coming here, competing in their conditions and taking the trophy back home makes the achievement even more meaningful,” he said.The series victory provides another significant boost for Indian lawn bowls in what has already been a successful year for the sport and will serve as a confidence booster ahead of upcoming international competitions, including the World Championships.
Article Summary: India complete remarkable turnaround to clinch three-match lawn bowls series against New Zealand with a 3-2 victory in the deciding test at Royal Oak Bowls in Auckland on Wednesday. The triumph completed a stunning recovery after India lost the opening test and found themselves adapting to unfamiliar conditions in Auckland.

Article Title: Venugopal Rao: 'Built a cricket ecosystem from scratch, now ready for the next chapter'
Article Text:
Venugopal Rao, Delhi Capitals former director of cricket. speaks to Sameer Rizvi after a net session during the IPL 2025 at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi. (ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Former India cricketer Venugopal Rao says he is "happy" and "content" when asked what's next for him after ending his four-and-a-half-year association with GMR Group 's cricket franchises, where he served as Director of Cricket."I am in Hyderabad, enjoying my time away from cricket. Now I'm taking some time out to be with my family. My kids have also been asking for my time, so that's important," Rao tells TimesofIndia.com.The 44-year-old has been the architect of the GMR Group's cricketing operations across the globe. He played a pivotal role in guiding Dubai Capitals to the ILT20 title in 2025 and was appointed Delhi Capitals' Director of Cricket for the 2025 and 2026 IPL seasons. He also joined Seattle Orcas as General Manager of Cricket Operations and has helped steady the ship at Southern Brave in The Hundred, a franchise in which the GMR Group has invested heavily."For four-and-a-half years, I was involved day in and day out, setting up the entire system. When I came in, nothing was in place. I built the whole cricket ecosystem, brought people in, and they did well," he says."But I will definitely get involved with teams and do something in cricket again. I can't keep myself away from the game for too long. For the next four or five months, I'll take some time and see what happens. I'm looking forward to opportunities and will see where things go," adds Rao, a veteran of 121 first-class matches.Under Venugopal Rao and head coach Hemang Badani, the Delhi-based franchise finished fifth and sixth in IPL 2025 and 2026, respectively. Sourav Ganguly has now been appointed as Delhi Capitals' head coach ahead of IPL 2027. The move follows the agreement reached between DC co-owners GMR Sports India Pvt Ltd and JSW Sports, under which the two partners would alternate control of the franchise's operations in two-year cycles.“When you look back at our first season (IPL 2025), especially the two games against Mumbai Indians, one at home and one away, I think we could have won both. In the first game in Delhi, we had four or five run-outs, which cost us the match. Karun played a superb knock, and we could have chased the target comfortably. Even in the Mumbai game, we had four or five run-outs, which again cost us," Rao reflects."In the Mumbai game, Axar Patel missed out due to illness. If you look at the surface, it was turning, and Mitchell Santner was a crucial bowler for them who picked up an important wicket. Axar was a big miss for us, not just with the ball but also while batting. As a left-hander, he would have been better equipped to tackle left-arm spin."Those were the two games in our first season that we missed out on, and winning them could have helped us qualify for the knockouts."Rao feels that even in the second season, in 2026, they were in contention for the playoff spots and could have qualified with a bit of luck."Even in the second season, if you look back at the home game against Gujarat Titans, David Miller was on strike. We needed two runs off two balls, but we couldn't win the game. That was our biggest disappointment. A player like Miller should have finished that game," he says."There was also the game against Punjab in which we scored 265. A lot of people say we should have defended that total, but if you look at the circumstances, Lungi Ngidi got injured and had to go to the hospital. That cost us around four hours. At the same time, we dropped eight catches."Normally, if you score 265 and drop eight catches, it's difficult to defend that total. If we had won those two games, Gujarat would have finished in the top two. That's how the IPL works, and we had to accept it," he adds.On the debate over whether Axar Patel or KL Rahul should lead Delhi Capitals (DC), Rao believes the incoming leadership should be allowed to operate without interference.“Whoever takes over should be given a free hand. Whether it’s Axar or KL, both have played at this level and understand the game. I have always believed in giving people freedom. Mistakes can happen, but your intentions should be good. If they are, you should have the clarity and freedom to take decisions," he says.Rao cites KL Rahul's turnaround as an example. After a slow start in IPL 2024, Rahul finished as the franchise's leading run-scorer, amassing 539 runs that season and 593 in IPL 2025."We backed KL Rahul and gave him a particular role. From the first season to the second, we worked on building his confidence. We told him he would have our support, and that was important. He delivered. He told us that if we backed him, he would deliver the results, and he did," he says.Rao also stressed that backing the coaching staff and management is central to building a successful franchise. Citing Chennai Super Kings' turnaround after a difficult 2020 season and RCB's consistency in reaching the playoffs before winning the title in 2025, he said teams needed to trust their cricketing personnel and allow them to work."The difference between teams that win championships and those that don't is often the support staff, the processes and the freedom given to people. Miracles may happen occasionally, but consistency is what helps teams win trophies and matches. Look at teams like CSK, Mumbai Indians and Kolkata Knight Riders. When the management gives people a free hand, it makes a difference."I still remember Chennai Super Kings having a difficult season in 2020. They didn't finish in the top four, but from what I heard from MS Dhoni, he maintained the same atmosphere in the dressing room and didn't allow outside interference. The following season, they won the trophy."You can see something similar with Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB). The hard work over three years helped them consistently qualify for the playoffs. When I spoke to Faf du Plessis, who was with us at DC, he told me that the cricketing decisions were largely left to the cricketers.The management was involved, but the cricketing people had the freedom to do their job."In franchise cricket, you often see the difference when the people responsible for cricket are allowed to take decisions. There is a lot of noise on social media, with people asking teams to change this or that. But if you keep interfering, the franchise will always struggle to build consistency," he adds.
Article Summary: Former India cricketer Venugopal Rao says he is "happy" and "content" when asked what's next for him after ending his four-and-a-half-year association with GMR Group's cricket franchises. He played a pivotal role in guiding Dubai Capitals to the ILT20 title in 2025 and was appointed Delhi Capitals' Director of Cricket for the 2025 and 2026 IPL seasons. He also joined Seattle Orcas as General Manager of Cricket Operations.

Article Title: Sandpapergate fallout: Usman Khawaja, David Warner pulled from commentary duties amid fresh storm
Article Text:
Former Australian cricketers Usman Khawaja, left, and David Warner. (AP Photo)

Khawaja, Bancroft revelations reignite Sandpapergate

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cummins rejects allegations as CA backs captain

The fallout from Australia's explosive Sandpapergate controversy has taken another turn, with broadcaster Fox Cricket taking former openers Usman Khawaja and David Warner off its commentary roster as fresh revelations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal continue to rock Australian cricket.Fox Sports managing director Steve Crawley confirmed that both commentators would be rested from broadcasts over the next few weeks, acknowledging that the continuing controversy had made it increasingly difficult for them to concentrate on their broadcasting responsibilities. No return date has been announced.“In light of recent events, both Usman and Davey will be rested from our broadcasts over the next few weeks,’’ Crawley told CODE Sports.“While we always support all members of our commentary team and welcome a diversity of views, which is a feature of our summer of cricket, we also understand the pressure they are under to respond to every new comment," he added.“We think it is increasingly difficult to focus on the game while the situation continues to unfold and think it is unfair on both commentators to put them in that position," he said.“Our focus remains on providing our viewers with the best broadcast of Australia’s summer of cricket.We will continue to monitor the situation," he concluded.The controversy has resurfaced following revelations in Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr, and subsequent comments from Cameron Bancroft suggesting that knowledge of the ball-tampering plan extended beyond the three players who were initially sanctioned.Bancroft was caught using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball during the Cape Town Test against South Africa in March 2018. The scandal resulted in suspensions for then captain Steve Smith, vice-captain Warner and Bancroft, triggering one of the biggest crises in Australian cricket.In his autobiography, Khawaja questioned the extent of knowledge within the Australian dressing room about the plan. Bancroft subsequently added fuel to the controversy through a column in The West Australian, alleging that the wider squad was aware of what was happening and that discussions about generating reverse swing had involved members of the bowling group, includingPat Cummins .Bancroft described Cummins' recent press conference as the 'final straw' that prompted him to break his silence.Cummins strongly rejected the allegations when questioned about them in Sydney, describing the suggestion that the entire team knew about the plan as "complete and utter nonsense".The renewed controversy has put Australia's Test captain under scrutiny, with questions emerging over his position amid the fresh claims. Cricket Australia, however, has backed Cummins to continue as skipper, issuing a statement of support.Australia face England in the first of five T20 Internationals at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Saturday, before opening their home Test summer against New Zealand at Perth Stadium on December 9.
Article Summary: Usman Khawaja and David Warner have been taken off Fox Cricket's commentary roster. Fox Sports managing director Steve Crawley confirmed that both commentators would be rested from broadcasts over the next few weeks. No return date has been announced. The controversy has resurfaced following revelations in Khawja's autobiography, Sabr, and subsequent comments from Cameron Bancroft. Cricket Australia has backed captain Pat Cummins to continue as skipper.

Pakistan have announced their much-delayed central contracts for 38 players, with former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood , along with opener Imam-ul-Haq , among the notable omissions from the new list released by the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Saturday.The announcement comes after a considerable delay, with the previous central contracts having expired on June 30. The PCB has introduced a new format-based structure, dividing players into separate Test, ODI and T20 categories, alongside a development category that accommodates the majority of the contracted players.The exclusions of Rizwan, Shan and Imam come amid recent setbacks in their international careers. Shan was recently removed as Pakistan's Test captain, while Rizwan and Imam were sent back home from England during Pakistan's tour, following which the visitors suffered a 3-0 whitewash in the Test series.Former captain Shadab Khan has also seen his status reduced, receiving a contract only in the T20 category.Test captain Babar Azam and Salman Ali Agha are the only two players included in the combined Test and ODI category. ODI captain Shaheen Shah Afridi has been placed in the ODI/T20 category, while Sahibzada Farhan, who led Pakistan in their most recent T20 Internationals, has received a contract exclusively in the T20 category.Among the other notable omissions are all-rounder Aamer Jamal, Saim Ayub, young pacer Akif Javed and spinner Ali Usman. Pacers Khurram Shahzad and Mohammad Ali, who recently toured the West Indies and England, have also been left out.The PCB has awarded contracts to 38 players but has not disclosed the remuneration attached to the individual categories.The newly introduced development category has the largest representation, with 19 players included.

Rahul, Gill and Pant put India in command

NEW DELHI: India's batting firepower came to the fore in the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington as the visitors scripted a piece of history, with all their top five batters scoring fifty-plus in the same innings in an away Test for the first time. A magnificent century from KL Rahul and valuable contributions from the rest of the top order put India firmly in the driver's seat, with a substantial 118-run lead at stumps on Day 3.After New Zealand posted a competitive 368 in their first innings, India responded with a commanding batting display, reaching a position of strength with two days remaining in the contest. The visitors' top five ensured there were no easy breakthroughs for the hosts, with every batter making a significant contribution to the first-innings total.The landmark achievement had previously occurred only four times in India's Test history, with all four instances coming on home soil. The Wellington Test against New Zealand in 2026 therefore became the first occasion when India's first five batters crossed the half-century mark in an overseas Test innings.The historic effort was headlined by Rahul, who produced a patient and assured 136 off 290 deliveries, striking nine fours and two sixes.The opener's innings was particularly significant as he completed a century in all four SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia), underlining his credentials as one of India's most accomplished overseas batters. Yashasvi Jaiswal provided the perfect platform at the other end with an aggressive 85 off 89 balls, including 16 boundaries. Devdutt Padikkal continued the momentum with a composed 80 off 175 deliveries, striking 10 fours.Captain Shubman Gill came agonisingly close to another Test hundred, scoring 98 off 146 balls. His innings featured nine fours and two sixes before New Zealand pacer Jacob Duffy outsmarted him in the final over of the day.Rishabh Pant remained unbeaten on 55 off 62 balls, switching gears impressively after a cautious start. Having managed just 15 runs off his first 37 deliveries, the wicketkeeper-batter accelerated dramatically, scoring 37 off his next 18 balls to complete his half-century.India enjoyed a particularly productive third day, adding 142 runs in the final session despite losing two wickets. Rahul and Padikkal had earlier ensured a wicketless morning session, frustrating the New Zealand attack with their composure and shot selection.However, Kyle Jamieson produced a superb delivery to end Padikkal's promising innings, hitting the top of off stump. Rahul subsequently departed after making the mistake of playing away from his body, bringing an end to a knock that had put India in a commanding position.Gill and Pant then ensured New Zealand could not capitalise on those breakthroughs. While Gill looked set for a hundred, Duffy denied him at 98 in the final over.India will resume Day 4 with a 118-run advantage and six wickets in hand. The visitors will be keen to extend their lead beyond 250 before putting New Zealand under pressure in the fourth innings.The hosts face an uphill task to turn the contest around, although their dramatic one-run victory over England at Wellington in 2023 serves as a reminder that this venue can produce remarkable Test finishes.
Article Summary: India's top five score fifty-plus in an away Test for the first time. A magnificent century from KL Rahul and contributions from the rest of the top order put India firmly in the driver's seat. New Zealand posted a competitive 368 in their first innings, India responded with a commanding batting display.

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The competition featured 18 sports, with more than 20 world records reportedly set during the seven-day event.China topped the medal table with 435 medals, including 207 gold, while hosts Japan finished second with 186 medals — 64 gold, 60 silver and 62 bronze.Uzbekistan emerged as the third-ranked nation, collecting 145 medals, including 45 gold.India's fourth-place finish was particularly significant given the size of its contingent. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated the Indian contingent on its record performance, saying the achievement reflected the athletes' hard work, perseverance and self-belief.In a post on X, Murmu said the unprecedented medal haul would inspire young people to dream big, work with dedication and remain positive in the face of challenges. She also extended her congratulations to the entire Indian contingent.Para athletics was India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. Para badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze.India also won 11 medals in para swimming, seven in para table tennis, six in para archery and five in para shooting. The Aichi-Nagoya edition was the fifth staging of the event, with Doha, Qatar, scheduled to host the sixth in 2030.For India, the closing ceremony marked the end of a historic campaign — one that raised the country's medal benchmark and showcased the depth and growing strength of its para-sport movement.

The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023.The achievement was particularly significant as India competed with a contingent of 168 athletes, nearly half the size of the squad that represented the country in Hangzhou.India remained fourth in the standings at the end of its campaign, although the final positions could change after a few remaining events on Saturday.Athletics remained India's biggest medal contributor, accounting for 65 medals, 12 more than at the previous edition. On Friday, however, the spotlight was shared with a superb badminton campaign and gold-winning performances in shooting and archery. Star javelin thrower Sumit Antil led an Indian 1-2-3 finish in the men's F42-44/61-64 combined event . The reigning Paralympic and world champion threw 72.46m to defend his title, while Mahendra Gurjar took silver with 59.03m and Sandip Sanjay Sargar claimed bronze with 64.48m. Gurjar finished ahead of Sargar on Raza points, which determine rankings in combined-classification events.Pranav Soorma added another gold in the men's club throw F51, defending his title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m. Dharambir secured bronze with 27.71m.Sandeep delivered a world-record performance in the men's 400m T64, clocking 52.28 seconds for gold. India's Ajay Kumar also reached the podium, winning bronze in a Games-record time of 53.61 seconds.Haney produced another world record, throwing 60.49m to win the men's javelin F37/38 title. India also picked up silver medals through Nimisha Chakkungalparambil in the women's long jump T47 and Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46, where he clocked 4:09.65.India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar and Games debutant Naveen Sivakumar.Nitesh defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles SL3 final. He later added a silver medal in mixed doubles SL3-SU5 alongside Thulasimathi Murugesan.Naveen, meanwhile, defeated Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 to win the men's singles SL4 title. Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own , combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.
Article Summary: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin 1-2-3 as Pranav Soorma strikes gold again

Sumit Antil and Pranav Soorma (ANI/PTI Photo)

Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep

Pranav Soorma defends club throw crown

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep at the Asian Para Games. Pranav Soorma defends his title in the men's club throw F51 event. Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar complete all-Indian podium finish.

NEW DELHI: Double gold medallists Mona Agarwal and Nishad Kumar will be India's flag-bearers at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, following outstanding campaigns in shooting and para-athletics.Both athletes won two gold medals each at the continental event, with Mona producing a record-breaking performance in shooting and Nishad excelling in the high jump and long jump.Their selection as flag-bearers recognises their achievements as India prepare to bring the Games to a close.The 38-year-old Mona opened India's medal account in shooting by winning gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games-record score of 250.0 points.
