He cleared 2.04 metres to set a new Games record in the latter event.The double-gold performance placed Nishad among a select group of Indian athletes to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games, joining para-runner Ankur Dhama and armless archer Sheetal Devi.Nishad's journey to the top has been marked by resilience. His right arm was severed by a grass-cutting machine at his family's farm in Himachal Pradesh when he was six years old. He went on to establish himself as one of India's leading para-athletes, particularly in the high jump.With two gold medals apiece, Mona and Nishad will lead India's contingent at Saturday's closing ceremony, providing a fitting conclusion to their impressive campaigns in Aichi-Nagoya.

Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan
Article Text:
Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

NEW DELHI: Thulasimathi Murugesan produced a memorable triple-medal performance at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Friday, winning gold and two silver medals as India's para-badminton contingent enjoyed a productive day in Aichi-Nagoya.The 24-year-old Paris Paralympics silver medallist capped her campaign with gold in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 event, partnering Manasi Joshi to defeat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final. The Indian pair wrapped up the contest in just 28 minutes.Thulasimathi had earlier settled for silver in the women's singles SU5 final, losing 18-21, 11-21 to China's Yang. She then teamed up with Nitesh Kumar in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, but the Indian combination went down 21-11, 19-21, 14-21 to Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.Nitesh, the Paris Paralympic champion, enjoyed a successful day of his own, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver with Thulasimathi.The 31-year-old defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles final."Last time I was close, I was leading 19-16 in the third set, and then I lost. So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Making his Asian Para Games debut, Naveen completed the win in 36 minutes.Pramod had to settle for silver after winning gold in the 2018 and 2022 editions. India's Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan also claimed silver in the women's singles SH6 final after losing to China's Li Fengmei.India continued to collect medals across disciplines on Friday. Para shooter Mona Agarwal won her second gold of the Games in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final, setting a world record with 357.5 points. Jehan Madan and Shubham Wadhwa secured bronze in men's doubles para table tennis MD4.India's tally stood at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with the country fourth in the standings. The contingent is chasing its best-ever Asian Para Games haul of 108 medals, achieved at Hangzhou in 2023.

Paris Paralympic silver medallist defeats China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in women's doubles final. Nitesh Kumar wins gold in men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver. India's tally stands at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with country fourth in standings.

India's Thulasimathi Murugesan added another medal to her growing collection at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, settling for silver in the women's singles SU5 badminton event after losing to China's Yang Qiuxia in the final on Friday. The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events. Her silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics marked a major milestone in her career, while her performances at the Asian Para Games have further strengthened her standing on the international stage.She trains in Hyderabad under coaches Pullela Gopichand and Irfan Sait while pursuing a degree in veterinary science at Namakkal. Article Title: Even €300M isn’t enough: Bayern Munich declare €60M signing Michael Olise unsellable despite persistent Real Madrid links
Article Text:
Munich's Michael Olise celebrates scoring during the Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and VfL Wolfsburg in Munich, Germany, Sunday Jan. 11, 2026. (Sven Hoppe/dpa via AP)

Bayern Munich reject €300m offer for Michael Olise

Herbert Hainer reveals what Florentino Perez told him about Real Madrid

Bayern's Michael Olise, centre, celebrates with Bayern's Harry Kane, left, and Bayern's Luis Diaz after scoring his side's third goal during the German soccer cup match between VfL Osnabrueck and Bayern Munich in Osnabrueck, Germany, Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Martin Meissner)

Michael Olise's Bayern Munich career, trophies and individual awards

Real Madrid may have the financial muscle to pursue almost any player in European football, but Bayern Munich have made it clear that Michael Olise is not for sale. Club president Herbert Hainer has dismissed the possibility of accepting even a €300 million offer for the French winger, insisting Bayern would rather build their future around him than turn his performances into a transfer profit. With Olise flourishing in Germany and Real Madrid repeatedly linked with him, Hainer has also offered an important clarification about the Spanish club's interest.Speaking to German publication t-online, Hainer ruled out selling Olise regardless of the size of a potential offer, making clear that Bayern have no intention of negotiating his departure.“We are not a selling club, we are a buying club,” Hainer said, echoing a familiar stance previously expressed by former Bayern chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge. The Bayern president stressed that the club's approach had not changed, insisting that transfer decisions could not be judged purely on financial terms.“You can't always just look at the financial aspect. You also have to consider whether the player is a good fit for us – in terms of playing style, personality, character traits, and also as a person,” Hainer explained.His comments underlined Bayern's determination to retain Olise, whose importance to their attacking plans goes beyond his potential transfer value.Hainer also dismissed suggestions that the Frenchman might be tempted to leave the Bundesliga champions, adding: “Michael feels at home here and knows what he has at FC Bayern.”The 24-year-old France international is contracted to Bayern until June 2029, and his agreement contains no release clause. That leaves the German club in a strong position to resist approaches, with Hainer confident that Olise has little reason to seek an exit.Real Madrid have repeatedly been linked with Olise, with reports suggesting the Spanish giants pursued the winger during the previous summer transfer window. Hainer has now provided his account of a conversation with Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, which took place when the Bayern chief attended a graduation ceremony at the Spanish club's university school.According to Hainer, Perez assured him that Real Madrid had never held discussions with Olise or his representatives about a potential transfer.“He assured me that Real Madrid had never held talks with Michael Olise or his agent,” Hainer said.The comments challenge speculation that negotiations had taken place between the Spanish club and the player's camp, although they do not rule out Real Madrid's admiration for the winger or future interest.Hainer had already taken a firm position in June 2026, when he publicly addressed the possibility of an approach from Perez.“If Florentino wants to send us an offer, which has not happened to date, he can save himself the trouble,” he said.His latest comments leave little ambiguity about Bayern's intentions: Olise is regarded as a player to build around, not an asset the club is prepared to sell, even for a fee that would rank among the biggest in football history. Hainer also highlighted the quality of Bayern's attack, declaring that the club currently have one of the best attacking trios in world football with Harry Kane, Olise and Luis Díaz.Olise joined Bayern from Crystal Palace on July 7, 2024, for a reported €60 million, approximately $65 million, including add-ons. He signed a five-year contract running until June 30, 2029, and has since developed into one of the most productive players in the Bundesliga.Across 122 appearances in all competitions, the Frenchman has recorded 54 goals and 55 assists, averaging almost one direct goal contribution per appearance. His influence has extended beyond individual numbers, with Bayern winning consecutive Bundesliga titles in 2024-25 and 2025-26.Olise also helped the club win the DFB-Pokal in 2025-26 and the 2025 German Supercup, bringing his major domestic trophy collection with Bayern to four. He was named Bayern's Player of the Season in both 2024-25 and 2025-26, won the 2025-26 Bundesliga Player of the Season award and finished ninth in the 2026 Ballon d'Or voting.His development in Germany followed three seasons at Crystal Palace, where he scored 16 goals in 90 appearances between 2021 and 2024. He had previously progressed through Reading's youth system before establishing himself in English football, making his move to Palace an important step towards the player Bayern eventually signed.Olise's rise has also strengthened his standing with France, where he has become an established international option. At 24, he is already a major part of Bayern's present and long-term plans, which explains why Hainer is so reluctant to entertain the possibility of selling him.
Article Summary: Bayern Munich reject €300m offer for Michael Olise. Club president Herbert Hainer reveals what Florentino Perez told him about Real Madrid's interest. Hainer insists Bayern would rather build their future around Olise than turn his performances into a transfer profit. Real Madrid have repeatedly been linked with the French winger.
